cases.answer: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) did raise the target range for the federal funds rate at the December 2022 meeting. The new target range is 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent, as stated in the minutes released on 2023-01-04 [2022-12-14/policyAction/3]. This was the 7th increase since March 16, 2022, with no cuts in between, resulting in a net change of 4.25 percentage points. The committee voted unanimously (12 members) to raise the rate. [the minutes 2022-12-14/policyAction/3]

cases.question: What was the outcome of the FOMC's December 2024 rate meeting?
cases.answer:
Apologies for the oversight. The FOMC decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent at the December 2024 meeting. They voted unanimously to lower the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.4 percent, effective December 19, 2024. [the decision record]

cases.question: Did the Committee change the target range for the federal funds rate at the September 2026 meeting?
cases.answer: The Committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate at the September 2026 meeting. The new range is 3-3/4 to 4 percent, an increase of 0.25 percentage points from the previous 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent. This was the first increase since July 26, 2023, following six cuts totaling 1.75 percentage points from September 18, 2024, to December 10, 2025. The latest minutes (released October 7, 2026) show unanimous agreement among members to raise the rate. [2026-09-16/policyAction/1]

cases.question: What was the target range for the fed funds rate in November 2015?
cases.answer: The target range for the federal funds rate in November 2015 was 0.25% to 0.50%, with the current rate at 0.25%. This was reaffirmed by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) at the October 28, 2015 meeting, as stated in [2015-10-28/policyAction/13] and [2015-10-28/policyAction/5]. The Committee noted that the current target range had remained appropriate and that they would assess whether to raise it at the next meeting, considering economic progress and uncertainties.

cases.question: What was the target range for the fed funds rate in February 2018?
cases.answer: In February 2018, the target range for the federal funds rate was 1.5% to 1.75%. This was the range decided upon by the FOMC at its December meeting, as indicated in the minutes released on February 21, 2018 [2018-01-31/staffFinancial/2, [2018-01-31/policyAction/5]]. The top of the range (1.5%) and bottom of the range (1.25%) were in place as of March 6, 2018 [2018-01-31/staffFinancial/2, [2018-01-31/policyAction/5]].

cases.question: What was the target range for the fed funds rate in February 2023?
cases.answer: The target range for the federal funds rate was raised to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent at the meeting that ended on 2023-02-01. This decision was unanimous, with 12 members voting in favor. The effective federal funds rate was 4.57% on that date, compared to 3.78% three months earlier and 0.08% a year earlier. The top of the target range was 4.75% on 2023-03-06, up from 4% three months earlier, and the bottom was 4.5%, unchanged from three months earlier. [2023-02-01/policyAction/19]
